previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with secondary progressive multiple sclerosis and neurogenic bladder managed with a chronic Foley catheter, was admitted for weakness and fever. He was diagnosed with acute pyelonephritis due to a catheter-related E. coli infection, confirmed by urine culture. He was initially treated with vancomycin and cefepime, transitioned to Unasyn temporarily due to sensitivity concerns, then resumed cefepime when testing confirmed susceptibility. A PICC line was placed to complete a 14-day course of IV antibiotics at home. Imaging revealed bladder calculi, which were discussed with urology for planned outpatient removal to reduce recurrent infection risk. The patient had fecal incontinence with stool soiling of the catheter site and was managed with home health services for weekly catheter changes. He remained clinically stable, with resolution of fever and infection, and was discharged home on IV cefepime, methenamine, and vitamin C for UTI prophylaxis, with follow-up arranged.
problems: Infection and inflammatory reaction due to indwelling urinary catheter
Acute pyelonephritis without lesion of renal medullary necrosis
Other and unspecified Escherichia coli [E. coli]

has been discharged on a seven day course of

Neurology follow-up has been scheduled.

# Pressure ulcers: 
Left trochanteric and right gluteal wounds, likely pressure

Wound care recommendations were included in discharge 
information; patient will likely require continued wound care.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ male with a history of secondary progressive MS and
report of intrathecal baclofen pump that is not able to be appreciated on
physical exam.

STUDY:  Supine abdominal radiograph.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  A pump device projects over the left hemi-abdomen with a catheter
extending toward midline and extending up the expected course of the spinal
canal.  Its appearance is unchanged from prior exam.  Extensive stool is seen
both in the rectum and colon.  There are no dilated loops of bowel. 
Assessment for free air is limited on this supine view.  Clips along the left
hemipelvis are unchanged.  Degenerative changes are present in the left hip.

IMPRESSION:  Intrathecal pump and catheter positioning in stable appearance;
extensive colonic fecal burden as described above.
